citeAs: Mathew, Minesh, Dimosthenis Karatzas, and C. V. Jawahar (2021). DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. WACV.
creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C. V. Jawahar (CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad; Computer Vision Center, UAB)
description: DocVQA is a visual question answering dataset on document images. It comprises 50,000 questions and answers defined on 12,767 document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, with questions requiring understanding of text, layout, tables, forms, figures, and other document structure.
name: DocVQA
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process included verification in a second stage by a different worker and a third-stage author review for cases where none of the first-stage answers exactly matched any second-stage answer. Questions flagged as inapt because of language issues or ambiguity were excluded from the dataset.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was organized in three stages. In stage 1, remote workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs, were encouraged to add more than one ground-truth answer when warranted, and were instructed to ask questions answerable using text present in the image and to enter the answer verbatim from the document. In stage 2, another worker answered the questions without seeing stage-1 answers, assigned one or more question types, and could flag inapt questions due to language issues or ambiguity. In stage 3, questions whose first- and second-stage answers did not exactly match were reviewed by the authors, who could edit or accept/ignore them.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset design prioritizes non-binarized document images and pages containing tables, forms, lists, and figures over pages with only running text, which biases the dataset toward better-quality images and structurally rich document pages. The authors also note that most documents are from the 1960-2000 period and that they used many documents from food and nutrition related collections because these had a good number of non-binarized images.
rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The authors downloaded documents from different collections, hand-picked pages for use in the dataset, minimized binarized images to avoid poor image quality, and prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists, and figures over pages containing only running text. Questions and answers were then collected from remote workers in a three-stage annotation process.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw source data are document images from 6,071 industry documents in the UCSF Industry Documents Library, spanning multiple decades and industries, including typewritten, printed, handwritten, and born-digital documents.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents used in the dataset range from 1900 to 2018.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: Existing models show a large performance gap compared to human performance, especially on questions where understanding document structure is crucial. The paper also notes challenges from OCR imperfections, difficulty with figures, photographs, and handwriting, and that document images often contain very large amounts of text.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors hand-picked pages from downloaded UCSF Industry Documents Library documents, tried to minimize binarized images because of poor image quality, and prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists, and figures over pages with only running text. The dataset was then split randomly into train, validation, and test sets in an 80-10-10 ratio.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for visual question answering on document images and to support research on purpose-driven document analysis and recognition, including methods that jointly use textual and visual cues such as layout, structure, forms, tables, and figures.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A Web based annotation tool was used for human annotation, and a commercial OCR application was used to extract OCR tokens used in analysis and experiments.
